Its retained Einstein term, absence of assumed scalar slow roll and optional added potential are explicit; its later-evolution component is not absorbed into this role.

destinations.title: How does microphysically motivated dissipation change inflationary dynamics, primordial spectra and supersymmetric model building for monomial, hybrid and hilltop potentials? This invited review also extends earlier model analyses.

Can inflation controlled partly by growing quantum fluctuations satisfy cosmological requirements while avoiding restrictions inferred from potential-driven evolution? The paper examines spinodal natural inflation while provisionally assuming two swampland conjectures.

Determine which geometric, potential and initial-condition assumptions are essential for rapid-turn inflation, and whether relaxing them permits models compatible with scalar observations and the particular quantum-gravity conjectures examined in the paper.

Do explicit fluctuation-control requirements similarly restrict inflation when extra degrees of freedom affect scalar dynamics, as in warm inflation, or when the inflating source is not a fundamental scalar? The paper identifies these questions without answering them.
The setting asks how a canonical inflaton evolves when brane gravity adds a quadratic energy-density contribution to the Friedmann equation and allows bulk gravitational effects.

Can the dilaton flow of a linear-expansion endpoint be used during an inflationary non-critical phase? The paper assumes the same coefficient in φ∝ln a while also imposing potential domination and q≈−1.
Can changes to the Friedmann equation allow a canonical inflaton to traverse an order-one field distance on a steep potential while producing sufficient inflation and acceptable spectra?
Can a small periodic correction produce enough inflaton quanta to slow a steep background? The correction enters both the homogeneous force and the time-dependent fluctuation mass.

Can a noncanonical tachyon inflaton and the high-energy RS-II expansion law jointly remove the distance, de Sitter, fluctuation-amplitude and horizon-entropy obstacles that the paper reviews for ordinary single-field inflation?

How does dissipative particle production realize warm inflation, support viable microscopic models, modify primordial perturbations, and permit compatibility with observations and swampland conjectures?
Can expansion-induced, out-of-equilibrium stress in a non-conformal QFT sustain exponential expansion while satisfying H ≪ M ≪ Msp, without a fundamental inflaton?

Can dissipation during inflation satisfy slow-roll and density-perturbation requirements with mφ≫H, η≫1 and sub-Planckian inflaton amplitudes, thereby avoiding the usual eta problem without symmetry protection of an exceptionally flat potential?
